digest.component_or_area: plan review: ac-satisfiability criterion and sibling-roster infrastructure
propositions: Plan review certified tickets with mutually unsatisfiable acceptance criteria across parent and children despite zero blocking findings, forcing expensive late-cycle LLM re-reviews when contradictions surface.

No existing plan-review criterion owns the coherence concern of whether a ticket's own acceptance criteria and Scope/Out-of-Scope declarations are jointly satisfiable, particularly for set-quantification primitives (universal-vs-carve-out, derived-artifact closure, snapshot cardinality).
G3's child-coverage audit cannot fire because it receives only child ids and titles; it needs each child's acceptance-criteria items to discharge the "no sibling covers it" test.

The sibling roster is constructed identically in three independent locations (pass1.py, fidelity_spot_eval.py, eval_solver.py), risking divergence between production and eval-harness paths and corrupting dogfooding data for G3's deferred posture decision.

The roster must move from per-pairing instructions into the byte-stable system-prompt prefix to avoid quadratic re-transmission with child count, and its token cost must be included in the parent_tokens estimate to preserve bin-packing and cache-gate correctness.
